arguments.direction_bridge: For fixed v != 0, openness gives theta0+tv in Theta for |t| small. Substitute h=tv in vector QMD: norm remainder=o(|t| ||v||)=o(|t|), derivative (v^T s)/2. Square integrability follows from |v^T s|² <= ||v||² ||s||². Restrict t>=0 to obtain the local DQM path; v=0 is constant. No converse from one path to full vector QMD is asserted.
arguments.centering_and_uniqueness: With q_t=q+t s q/2+r_t and ||r_t||=o(t), normalization gives 0=t Ps+2<q,r_t>+||t s q/2+r_t||². Cauchy-Schwarz makes the last two terms o(t), hence Ps=0. Subtract two expansions and divide by t/2 to obtain ||s-sprime||_L2(P)=0. This uses no assumed centering.
arguments.domination_and_choice: Both interfaces use one fixed supplied sigma-finite dominator and nonnegative RN density versions. Each norm is unaffected by separate null changes; no common null set or parameter measurability is asserted. Scalar definition explicitly retains AC for density-family selection; Hilbert branches retain Countable Choice for L2 completeness.
arguments.boundary_distinction: Interior QMD permits v and -v. A constrained boundary is handled separately by one-sided paths. Binary theta(t)>=0 forces right derivative a>=0; all a>=0 are realized by theta(t)=at for sufficiently small t. Scores form {aX:a>=0}; the real closed span is {bX:b in R}=L2_0(P0). No two-sided assumption is imported at the boundary.
arguments.bounded_score_example: For bounded centered s, a_t=1+ts/2 is positive for sufficiently small t; c_t=P a_t²=1+t²Ps²/4. The explicit density a_t²/c_t has root remainder norm |1-sqrt(c_t)|=O(t²). Centered truncations approximate every L2_0 class in L2, proving full tangent space without asserting every score is bounded.
arguments.regular_bernoulli: Positive interior masses permit two scalar square-root derivatives, giving scores 1/p and -1/(1-p); direct sums yield mean zero and variance 1/[p(1-p)].
arguments.closed_span: Finite real span is linear; ball approximations prove its norm closure linear and closed, and ambient completeness under Countable Choice gives a Hilbert subspace. Nuisance definitions specify designated paths with zero right target derivative and orthogonal complement inside L2_0(P).
